nodes.description: Impaired TLR3 signaling reduces cell-intrinsic induction of IFN-beta and IFN-lambda in non-hematopoietic cells (fibroblasts, cortical neurons, pulmonary epithelial cells), while circulating leukocytes retain TLR3-independent interferon responses.

nodes.description: Childhood HSV-1 encephalitis, the hallmark and often sole severe infectious episode.

evidence.reference_title: TLR3 deficiency in patients with herpes simplex encephalitis.
evidence.snippet: We report a dominant-negative TLR3 allele in otherwise healthy children with herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) encephalitis.

nodes.description: In the central nervous system, TLR3 is required for cortical-neuron-intrinsic type I interferon immunity to HSV-1; its loss leaves neurons unable to control viral replication.
In the lung, defective TLR3-dependent interferon responses in pulmonary epithelial cells permit uncontrolled influenza A replication, underlying severe pneumonitis and ARDS in a subset of patients.

Type I (IFN-alpha2b) and type III (IFN-lambda1) interferon rescue the cell-intrinsic antiviral defect in patient-derived cells in vitro, providing mechanistic rationale for interferon-based approaches; clinical use is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Severe influenza pneumonitis in children with inherited TLR3 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Treatment with IFN-α2b or IFN-λ1 rescues this phenotype.

nodes.description: Germline TLR3 variants abolish (recessive complete) or partially impair (dominant-negative) recognition of double-stranded RNA by the endosomal receptor TLR3, the initiating molecular lesion. TLR3-mutated fibroblasts do not respond to the synthetic dsRNA analog poly(I:C).
Unchecked HSV-1 replication and cell death in the CNS produce the tissue lesion of herpes simplex encephalitis.
